ports.note: A table in, a table of estimates out: one row per reported term with its ratio, interval limits and p. The design port is optional; a declared case-control design allows logistic regression only.

ontology.note: No ontology mapping yet. The receipt states the model in a sentence, every column of the design matrix in R's naming, the rows used and left out with reasons, strata used and dropped, the interval method and the estimates.

changes.description: Logistic and Poisson regression of an outcome on an exposure, adjusted for numeric, categorical (treatment-coded) and B-spline (R's bs()) terms, fitted by IRLS in the Rust kernel. Poisson takes an offset and strata absorbed as fixed effects. Intervals: likelihood-ratio (profile), Wald, Wald scaled for overdispersion, or HAC (Newey-West). Experiment 167.

evidence.note: Kernel unit tests: a two-by-two as logistic regression gives its odds ratio and Woolf's standard error; an unadjusted Poisson model gives the rate ratio; absorbed strata give the coefficients of the model with stratum indicators. Published figures reproduced on the authors' own data: NYC ozone 1.0609 per 10 ppb, coefficient and HAC standard error equal to the authors' archived R result to 12 significant figures; Salmonella Galia melon adjusted for age group (7 groups) and sex, 96 (15-2067) and 18 (4.6-101) against the published 96 (15-2100) and 18 (4.6-100). Nothing here establishes that a model is well specified.
